rows.subtype: Approach: builds a checklist after forgetting something important [Revision]
rows.description: After forgetting his admit card once, a student writes a list of documents and pens for every exam day and checks it the night before.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Approach: uses a checklist for a repeated multi-step process [Action]
rows.description: A lab assistant follows a checklist for setting up an experiment, so steps in the right order are not skipped even when tired or hurried.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Approach: ticks boxes without thinking, so the list hides new problems [Pitfall]
rows.description: A technician runs the usual checklist and signs off, but the new machine has a different fault that no line covers. The list gave false confidence.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Approach: reviews and updates the checklist after each incident [Revision]
rows.description: After a missed step in a client release, the team adds a line for it and removes two that no longer apply, so the list stays useful and short.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: impulsive action
this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Approach: pairs a trigger with an action [Action]
rows.description: A boy decides that if he sees his shoes by the door after school, then he puts them on the rack. The trigger reminds him without effort.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Approach: prepares an if-then reply to handle peer pressure [Thinking]
rows.description: A teenager plans that if friends offer to skip class, then he says he has a test and leaves. Deciding beforehand makes the words easier to say.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Approach: attaches a new habit to an existing cue [Action]
rows.description: A student decides that after brushing teeth in the morning, he revises five flashcards. The habit hooks onto an already stable routine.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Approach: writes so many rules that none can be recalled [Pitfall]
rows.description: A young manager makes dozens of if-then rules for her week. When a busy day comes she remembers none and reverts to reacting to the loudest request.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Approach: keeps three key if-then rules and revises them when they fail [Revision]
rows.description: She reduces to three rules, notices the after-lunch one is ignored, and moves the trigger to when she closes her laptop at four.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Approach: imagines the steps before acting, sometimes out loud [Thinking]
rows.description: A child about to carry a glass of water says out loud, walk slow, hold with two hands, put it down. Picturing the steps helps her avoid a spill.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
